newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam coffee farmers hold back as prices rise.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam coffee farmers hold back as prices rise.

text.p: Coffee farmers in Vietnam's main producing area, Dak Lak province, were holding back on selling beans on Friday as prices in London and New York looked set to continue rising, traders said.
They said trade had yet to recover following the recent Tet lunar new year festival, but farmers were also under little pressure to sell.
"They're just sitting back and taking it easy while the markets continue to rise. Business is stuck," one said.
Prices for Vietnam robusta were quoted at around $1,390 to $1,400 per tonne FOB Saigon Port, up from around $1,200 just ahead of the new year holiday in early February.
New York's CSCE future market saw coffee prices surge for the sixth straight session on Thursday with March coffee reaching a 21-month high on weekly charts.
Regional dealers said they expected prices in London to rise further when the market opened later on Friday.
"On numbers it's due $70 higher, but we expect about 35 up, It'll definitely rise today," said one trader.
Dealers estimate that Vietnam has sold about 150,000 tonnes of its 1996/97 coffee crop so far with a further 120,000 tonnes or so left to go.
